problem.statement: Taiwan's periodic dog-population surveys and research on mark-recapture imply an investigation requirement for repeatable sightings with photographic identity records; this is not a confirmed local agency procurement request.

sources.claim: Population estimation literature describes the importance of identification and repeat observation for free-roaming dog abundance estimation.
Taiwan's 2024 national dog estimate and periodic survey methodology do not establish a continuously tracked local population.

repository.description: Open-source form/data collection infrastructure for field operations and surveys.

fit.documented_capability: KoboToolbox provides offline forms and API access to survey records and attachments, potentially allowing dog sighting photos to be collected.
fit.problem_requirement: Repeated dog-specific sightings with location/time/photo provenance, individual reconciliation, and valid population-estimation assumptions.
fit.unverified_gap: A dog-identification model and statistical abundance estimator would remain separate; no end-to-end field proof or Taiwan authority willingness-to-pay has been established.

market.buyer_segment: Potential animal-control departments, shelters, research organizations and field survey contractors
